title: Starting the OS
instructions: Open Overview with F12 (or WrOS › Overview): your book at a glance. Esc returns to your manuscript. On the appliance, tty1 starts this interface after login.

title: Keyboard layout selection
instructions: Open Settings › Look and keyboard › Keyboard, then the keyboard layout wizard. Preview a layout in the test field. Press Enter within 15 seconds to keep it, or Escape to revert. Linux translates characters; WrOS never translates them twice.

title: Creating a novel
instructions: Create a new novel in a separate folder. This lesson observes successful creation in a separate directory rather than merely opening a dialog.

title: Writing and Markdown formatting
instructions: In the safe demo, type an original sentence. The actual manuscript editor, autosave and undo are used. Ctrl-Z reverses the edit; Ctrl-S saves.

title: Navigating scenes and chapters
instructions: In the safe demo outline, open the other scene with arrow keys and Enter. The lesson checks that the open document actually changes.

title: Using the corkboard
instructions: Open the real corkboard. Arrow keys move among scene cards. Escape returns without changing prose.

title: Switching workspaces
instructions: Open View › Workspaces… and choose another saved layout. Each workspace remembers its primary document position and outline settings.

title: Using focus mode
instructions: Enter strict focus mode with Ctrl-D. Only the manuscript remains. Ctrl-D restores the previous layout.

title: Managing panes
instructions: Show or hide the outline on its own: type toggle outline in Find anything (Ctrl+K) and press Enter, or bind it a key in Keyboard shortcuts. Tab only visits visible panes. F11 toggles an independent editor, taught in lesson 13; strict focus hides both side panes.

title: Custom keyboard shortcuts
instructions: Open Keyboard shortcuts and add a Ctrl+Alt letter alias. Existing bindings are protected. Instructions refer to logical letters under QWERTY, Colemak and Colemak-DH.

title: Sticky-note pins
instructions: In the safe demo, n opens the real source picker. Choose the shipped Pin Practice note (or another existing scene or note) and press Enter. The saved card references its original Markdown file; it contains no copied body. Only a successful pin save completes this exercise.

title: Scrolling inside sticky notes
instructions: In the safe demo Pinboard, choose the shipped Pin Practice card, whose The Courtyard heading is ready to use. Press h to capture the heading, PgDn to scroll the card, then Home to return to that unique semantic anchor. Only a real persisted anchored scroll-and-return completes this exercise; missing or duplicate headings are not guessed.

title: Editing notes beside the manuscript
instructions: In the safe demo, choose The Other Door in the secondary document picker and type an original sentence in that independent editor. Tab changes panes; each keeps its selection and undo. F11 hides without discarding it. Only a real edit in the secondary demo buffer completes this exercise.

title: Writing journal
instructions: In the safe demo, first type an original sentence in the manuscript and save it to produce a real automatic checkpoint. Open Tools › Notes › Writing journal… (or find it with Ctrl-K). Review its recorded facts, Tab to the separate reflection, Enter to edit its original, and write/save a personal reflection. Only an actual saved reflection after reviewing recorded facts completes this exercise; no gross-word or active-time estimates are invented.

title: Scratchpad
instructions: In the safe demo, open Scratchpad, n to create an original note, write/save an idea, reopen Scratchpad and l to link a manuscript scene. Press p to create one independent scene snapshot. The original note stays intact; a button or blank note cannot complete this lesson.

title: Session handoff
instructions: In the safe demo, open Session handoff, Enter to edit its ordinary original note, and write/save your next-session intention. Reopen Session handoff and s to arm next-open display with an optional saved manuscript context. Quit normally and reopen the same demo: seeing the actual saved original intention completes the exercise, not arming it alone.

title: Daily writing goals
instructions: Open Goals and change the daily or novel target in the demo. The lesson observes a saved target change, not just the dialog.

title: NaNoWriMo tracking
instructions: In the safe demo, open Calendar and rest days, press n for the explicit November 50k preset, then Space on a chosen date to record a real rest-day choice. Start/end, target, remaining-day pace and forecast assumptions are shown. Opening the page or pressing a Next button is not completion.

title: Sprints
instructions: Start a real writing sprint in the demo (Tools › Start a sprint…). The lesson observes an active sprint. No-editing and revision variants remain planned.

title: Achievements
instructions: In the safe demo, review the real optional milestone collection. If it is empty, return to a manuscript scene, type an original word with the keyboard and Ctrl-S to checkpoint the actual operation, then reopen Milestone collection. Only a nonempty recorded collection completes this review; no badge is fabricated by the lesson.

title: Daily challenges
instructions: In the safe demo, open Daily challenges and press a to accept the measured fifty-word drafting exercise before writing. Return to an actual manuscript scene in Drafting mode; add fifty source word units (typing or deliberate paste counts), Ctrl-S, reopen Daily challenges and press c. The lesson requires a persisted measured completion, not opening/rerolling a prompt or self-reporting a subjective task. Assignments survive restart and repeated local dates.

title: Story Spark plot generation
instructions: In the safe demo, open Story Spark from Tools › Practice or Find anything. Press 1 for plot-only, inspect the complete situation and v provenance, then s to create a saved Markdown note. Opening the view or generating alone is not completion; the lesson requires a real saved original source. No active scene is replaced.

title: Random writing challenges
instructions: In the safe demo, open Story Spark, press 2 for an independently usable exercise, and read its work mode. o edits future filters; Esc cancels without saving. Press f to favorite the exact exercise-only reference. The lesson requires a successfully persisted favorite, not opening a list or checking a fake completion button.

title: Combined plot-and-challenge roulette
instructions: In the safe demo, open Story Spark and press 3 for a compatible combined result. f favorites it; p changes only plot, e only exercise, and r changes both. Then a opens real result actions: create and open a NEW empty experimental scene. The source prompt is saved once in Notes; the new scene references it and is excluded from compile. Completion checks the persisted reroll chain, retained favorite, and successful independent scene creation. Static output works in focus/low-power; l is optional presentation-only roulette.

title: Dictionary and thesaurus
instructions: Open Dictionary and thesaurus… from Tools or Find anything. In the query field enter bank or hot, then press Enter to use the installed local WordNet 3.0 data. Wait for actual senses, choose a specific part-of-speech/sense and press Enter to read its real definition. That explicit sense review completes this lesson, not merely opening or typing a query. Tab switches synonyms and explicitly linked antonyms; a missing antonym is not invented. Copy is optional and never edits the manuscript; return through Escape to use normal selection/paste/undo if desired. Missing data is reported and never downloaded at runtime. This read-only exercise may be performed outside the demo.

title: Grammar and spelling
instructions: Open the existing spellcheck suggestions for a misspelled word in the demo. This historic completion records spelling, not grammar. Optional model-based Harper grammar and its ignore scopes are separate; lesson 40 requires a genuinely applied current original-demo grammar fix.

title: Hemingway-style highlighting
instructions: Run Prose and revision dashboard on original prose with r. p cycles the persisted Drafting, Revision and DeepReview profiles; f selects General, Accessible or Experimental fiction guidance. Read actual analysis-word/sentence/rhythm statistics, then press Enter to review them and open the queue. Opening, missing data and an empty/oversized source do not complete the exercise. The English readability approximation is not literary quality, native goal word units or authorship evidence.

title: Nabokov analysis
instructions: Use the Prose and revision dashboard. In your demo, a sentence such as The gate was opened by Mara. can demonstrate the passive pattern. Save it; choose Revision or DeepReview with p. d discloses the trained local spaCy pipeline; y permits ONE exact source/configuration run. No runtime downloads, detector rules or live opt-in. Review an actual returned Nabokov finding in the queue with Enter. A rewrite direction is never a literal replacement. Missing model/failed work/consent alone cannot complete this lesson. l explicitly controls dialogue-style relaxation.

title: Proselint
instructions: Run the pinned standalone non-model proselint adapter through r in Prose and revision dashboard. In the demo, He could of gone. can demonstrate a specialized usage finding. Inspect a real returned proselint finding in the queue with Enter, including equivalent-rule provenance. Merely running an empty/missing engine does not complete the lesson; quoted fictional dialogue is still prose. Corrections are optional and always explicit native Replace/Undo.

title: Author-style preservation
instructions: In Prose and revision dashboard choose v then n. Explicitly select your own saved original manuscript sources, not research or a repeated copy. Prepare and save a frozen numeric/reference baseline using at least 5,000 analysis words, 40 segments and one source with 150 distinct normalized words. A short demo is intentionally insufficient. Analyze at least 300 current words/five segments; return to v and press c to review the actual reference comparison. Saving, selecting or opening alone does not finish this exercise. Differences describe narrator/form/genre/intent, not literary quality or human authorship. No live rebase or manuscript copy is stored.

title: Continuity tracking
instructions: In the safe demo, open Continuity tracker… from Tools › Revision or Find anything. Press n to record an explicit character or world fact with a Subject, Property and Value, then press 4 (or c) to review Contradictions & Suggestions. Definite conflicts require two Definite facts sharing an explicit scope; unscoped changes suggest review without hallucinating contradictions. Optional: return to Facts, select the fact and press g to record a character's knowledge Before or After the active scene. Tab moves fields, Left/Right cycles state or point, Enter saves, 5 opens Character knowledge, v reviews retained versions, d archives and g opens the original source. These optional actions do not replace the lesson's actual fact-and-conflict review event.

title: Inline revision notes
instructions: In the safe demo, select an original passage and open Revision notes from the palette. Press n, write your own comment and Enter to save. Esc returns to writing. Edit that passage normally, then select its new wording. Reopen Revision notes, inspect your note with Enter, and press a. Review the old and new passages, choose Save reviewed anchor with Down and Enter. Only a changed anchor saved successfully completes this exercise. Opening, cancelling, resolving, or re-saving the same anchor does not count. Existing Undo, autosave and source history remain available; comments stay outside the manuscript.

title: Draft comparisons
instructions: Open Book › Scene history… (H) or Tools › Revision › Draft milestones… in the safe demo. Inspect a saved scene version, create a named milestone snapshot, or save a reversible scene variant. After editing, compare a saved milestone or variant. Left/Right chooses a changed passage and p opens complete current/saved wording. Cancel is selected initially. Explicitly choose Restore to change only that passage; Ctrl-Z in the original editor reverses it. Viewing or cancelling does not establish a successful restore.

title: Footnotes
instructions: In the safe demo, write a public Markdown reference such as Key[^key] and a separate definition paragraph [^key]: Your own note. Save normally. Read footnote at caret in Ctrl-K lets you inspect and edit the original definition. Open Export for readers, untick Paperback, and tick PDF. Word is included with PDF. Press p to review the selected source, Esc to return, then x to export. Only a successfully written manuscript Word file containing real notes followed by its completed nonempty PDF earns this exercise. Viewing notes, Word alone, unavailable LibreOffice, or a failed export cannot complete it. EPUB linked notes are available; EPUB alone does not earn the Word/PDF exercise. Paperback page notes remain unavailable; no external resource is fetched.

title: Exporting manuscripts
instructions: In the safe demo, open Export for readers through Ctrl-K. Untick Word and EPUB and tick Markdown. Press p to review the selected source; Esc returns to the export settings. Press x to export. If a TK warning appears, review it before pressing x again. Only a real nonempty Markdown file successfully written to exports/ completes this lesson. This does not verify Word/PDF/EPUB page footnotes.

title: Backing up and a test restore
instructions: Open Settings › Backups and accounts › Backups. Back up this book; WrOS checks each backup after it makes it, and later backs up on its own after you save and pause. Then pick a backup and restore it. It goes into a new folder beside your book, so nothing you have is replaced. Restore with settings also brings back the settings saved in that backup, after keeping your current ones. A finished restore completes this lesson. Backups to Google Drive need Drive linked first (lesson 41).

title: Reading your book on your phone
instructions: Open Settings › Backups and accounts › Backups and turn on sync for this book. WrOS keeps a plain copy of its scenes in your Google Drive, so the Drive app on your phone can open them. Edits you make there come back to WrOS; a paragraph changed in both places waits for you to merge it. Converting a scene to a Google Doc is not a safe round trip. A finished sync completes this lesson.

title: Wi-Fi and system settings
instructions: Open Settings › System. Wi-Fi, battery, brightness, storage and updates each have a page here. A service this computer lacks says so; it never pretends to work.

title: Recovery and troubleshooting
instructions: Open the offline History and recovery manual. It explains autosave, recovery and backups, and Ctrl+Alt+F2 for a maintenance console. If WrOS ever fails to start, restart and tap Esc as the laptop's logo goes, then choose WrOS recovery: it can show what happened, go back a version, or continue to the normal login. Nothing in this lesson touches your manuscript.

title: Optional local grammar: guarded review
instructions: Use this safe demo only. In its manuscript, type a deliberate article mistake such as I have a apple. Open Writing checks from the palette. Read the bundled-model disclosure; permission is optional, and declining leaves editing and spelling available. To perform this exercise, explicitly permit a single local check, wait for the AnA Grammar finding, inspect its original-source location, then press a to apply that exact current suggestion. Merely opening, consenting, navigating, ignoring or enabling live work is insufficient. A genuine grammar replacement in the original demo manuscript completes this additional lesson; Undo remains available. No preset text or consent is inserted by the lesson. You may skip it without penalty.

title: Linking Google Drive with your phone
instructions: Open Settings › Backups and accounts › Google Drive and choose Link Google Drive with your phone (or Relink). Scan the code with your phone's camera, sign in to Google and approve. If the phone asks, tap Finish linking. No second computer is needed. Linking finishes this lesson; you can relink at any time, and your book is not touched.

title: Warm screen
instructions: Open Settings › System › Display › Warm screen. Change the temperature or strength and preview it. The preview turns itself off after 15 seconds unless you choose Keep these display settings. Keeping a setting completes this lesson; it stays on after a restart.

title: Going back a version
instructions: Open Settings › Updates and recovery › Updates and choose Go back to the version listed there. WrOS keeps the version it installed before this one. The next screen offers it: going back installs at the next restart, and you can cancel until then. Stay on this version leaves everything as it is. Seeing that screen with a kept version completes this lesson. If an update ever fails to start twice, WrOS goes back on its own.

title: Finding Wi-Fi networks
instructions: Open Settings › System › Wi-Fi and networking and choose Scan Wi-Fi networks. Pick a network to join it. If the scan fails, the page says what to check. A finished scan completes this lesson.

title: Locking and sleep
instructions: Open Settings › System › Battery and power and choose Lock writing session. WrOS saves first, then asks for your password. Unlock to finish this lesson. Lock and suspend also puts the laptop to sleep. Lesson 46 covers the lid choice.

title: Choosing what the lid does
instructions: Open Settings › System › Battery and power. Choose When the lid closes to cycle through lock and sleep, lock and stay awake, and do nothing. Stop on the choice you want. Saving a choice finishes this lesson.

title: Battery warnings
instructions: In Battery and power, check the current charge. On battery, WrOS warns at 20% and 10%. At the 8% reserve it saves your words and counts down before locking and sleeping, if this laptop supports sleep. Plug in to stay awake. The next battery warning finishes this lesson.

title: Finding files on Google Drive
instructions: Open Settings › Backups and accounts › Google Drive. Link Drive first if you need to. Choose Your Drive files and wait for the folder to open. You can open another folder or copy a file to this laptop. Seeing a finished folder listing completes the lesson.

title: Practising a paragraph merge
instructions: Start this exercise in a safe demo. The merge panel shows two sample changes to one paragraph. Choose 1 for yours, 2 for Drive's, or 3 to keep both in that order. WrOS shows your practice result and finishes the lesson. Escape goes back so you can try again.

title: Using the start screen
instructions: Open Settings › System › Display and choose Start screen to switch between WrOS and plain text. Saving the choice finishes the lesson. The next restart uses that choice when preparation finishes. For one start only, press Esc at WrOS's graphical disk password prompt to use the plain prompt.
